faq.q: How do I even apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your bank's ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) facility via net banking, or through your stockbroker's platform. Your money remains in your bank account until shares are allotted.
A lot size is the minimum number of shares you must apply for in an IPO. You cannot apply for a single share; you must apply in multiples of the specified lot.

faq.q: What does it mean if an IPO is "oversubscribed"?
faq.a: If an IPO is oversubscribed, it means the company received applications for more shares than it offered. For example, if an IPO is subscribed 10 times, it means applications were received for 10 times the number of shares available.

Companies typically do IPOs to raise capital (money) for various reasons, such as funding expansion plans, paying off debts, investing in new projects, or allowing existing shareholders to sell their stake.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Mainboard IPO and an SME IPO?
faq.a: Mainboard IPOs are for larger, more established companies and are listed on the main exchanges (NSE, BSE). SME IPOs are for smaller companies and are listed on separate platforms like NSE Emerge or BSE SME, often with different regulatory requirements and minimum investment amounts.
